# s277 — TUI shows sibling-worktree claims and sibling-only items

The queue shows the same claim cell as `slicer list` (`owner`, `*`, `wt:NAME+N`, `-`) and ends with an "only in a sibling" block, so the owner sees from the TUI which slices other worktrees hold.

**Findings:** owner request, session 2026-10-14: bring the TUI up to date with recent CLI features · **Size:** S · **Tree:** slicer

**Not in this slice:** any write to a sibling worktree, and acting on sibling-only rows (they are read-only). The relay board (s283) is separate.

## Why

`View.refresh` already reads `store.in_work_elsewhere` (`src/slicer/tui.py:666`), but it only uses it to recolour a status. `item_rows()` (`src/slicer/tui.py:242`) has no claim column, and the detail pane shows only the local claim owner. `slicer list` prints the CLAIM column through `_claim_cell` (`src/slicer/cli.py:1568`) and the `Only in a sibling` block from `store.sibling_work` (`src/slicer/store.py:643`). With parallel relay worktrees, the TUI on `main` cannot tell what is being worked on elsewhere.

## Files

- `src/slicer/cli.py`: move `_claim_cell` (line 1568) to a module that both the CLI and the TUI may import, without changing its output.
- `src/slicer/tui.py`: `View.refresh` calls `store.sibling_work` once and keeps both halves; `item_rows()` adds the claim cell after status; `filtered_rows()` (line 572) appends a separator and non-selectable sibling-only rows (`ID  worktree  title`).
- `docs/tui.md` "Display and color", `CHANGELOG.md`.
- `tests/test_tui.py`, reusing the sibling fixtures in `tests/test_worktree_claims.py`.
